# About the Atlassian Rovo MCP Server

The Atlassian Rovo MCP Server is a cloud-hosted [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) server that connects AI-powered clients to your Atlassian Cloud apps. It provides a standardized interface for AI assistants, IDEs, and automation tools to read, create, and update work across Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Bitbucket, Loom, and the wider Atlassian platform - all secured by OAuth 2.1 authorization and your existing Atlassian permissions.

## What you can do

With the Atlassian Rovo MCP Server, AI clients can:

- **Search and summarize** Jira work items, Confluence pages, Bitbucket pull requests, and other Atlassian content without context switching.
- **Retrieve Loom recordings**, including transcripts, comments, AI briefs, and extracted meeting action items.
- **Create and update** work items, pages, and other content using natural language commands.
- **Automate repetitive work**, such as generating Jira work items from meeting notes or creating Confluence documentation from specs.
- **Query across apps** using Teamwork Graph, such as finding the pull requests, deployments, and documents connected to a work item.

## How it works

The MCP Server acts as a bridge between MCP-compatible clients and Atlassian Cloud APIs:

1. An AI client connects to the server endpoint at `https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp`.
2. The server initiates a secure OAuth 2.1 authorization flow (or accepts an API token for headless authentication).
3. Once authorized, the client can invoke tools to interact with Atlassian apps.
4. All actions respect the authenticated user's existing permissions - the server never grants access beyond what the user already has.

Rather than sending every tool definition at connection time, the server advertises a small set of **primary** tools and lets clients discover the rest of the catalog on demand through the `discover` tool. This preserves context window and lets Atlassian add tools without requiring you to reconnect. See [Supported tools](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/rovo-mcp/guides/supported-tools/) for details.

## Supported apps

| App | Capabilities |
|---|---|
| **Jira** | Search, create, edit, transition, and comment on work items; query spaces, boards, sprints, versions, and metadata |
| **Confluence** | Read, create, and update pages, live docs, whiteboards, and databases; search with CQL; manage comments, attachments, permissions, and spaces |
| **Jira Service Management** | Query and update ops alerts, on-call schedules, and team information |
| **Bitbucket Cloud** | Browse and act on repositories, pull requests, pipelines, deployments, and environments |
| **Loom** | Read and manage videos, transcripts, comments, meeting action items, and folders |
| **Goals, Projects, Focus areas, Teams, Talent** | Search, read, create, and update Atlassian platform work-tracking entities |
| **Teamwork Graph** | Retrieve connected context and relationships for any Atlassian entity |
| **Rovo Search** | Semantic search across Jira, Confluence, and connected apps using natural language |
| **Code search** | Search and read source code across connected code providers |

## Rovo credit usage

Some tools consume Rovo credits. Consumption depends on:

- **Context volume** - retrieving larger amounts of data costs more credits.
- **Reasoning depth** - complex queries consume more credits than simple lookups.
- **Usage caps** - per-call limits help manage cost. The vast majority of enriched TWG API and tool calls are 1-10 Rovo credits per call.

## Supported clients

The server works with any MCP-compatible client, including:

- [OpenAI ChatGPT](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
- [Claude Desktop and Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)
- [Docker](http://mcp.docker.com)
- [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/mcp-servers#_add-an-mcp-server)
- [Google Gemini](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/tools/mcp-server.md)
- [Amazon Quick Suite](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksuite/latest/userguide/mcp-integration.html)
- IDEs such as VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf
